text:
sara-support: Hey team — customer ACME reporting intermittent SchemaValidationError during streaming tool calls. Happens when tool args are large and we stream the tool_call event. Example error: "SchemaValidationError: Unexpected end of JSON input at position 512". They included raw stream segment where the JSON gets cut mid-object.

alan-eng: Can you paste the raw event stream & headers? suspect proxy/buffer split.

sara-support: Pasting redacted snippet from prod logs (SSE lines):

```
data: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"upload","params":{"path":"/backups/2025/aug/very_long_filename_01.tar.gz","meta":{"size":12457843,"checksum":"sha256:abc123..."}}

data: {"type":"tool_call_response","name":"upload","result":{"status":"ok","location":"https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme/objects/2025/aug/very_long_filename_01.tar.gz"}}

```

sara-support: but in the failing traces the second piece arrives truncated: `..."checksum":"sha256:abc123` (end-of-stream). Parser sees incomplete JSON and throws.

mike-ml: Are we emitting multiple SSE events for the args? Our runtime streams partial tokens which can split JSON payloads across events. If client tries to JSON.parse per event it will fail.

alan-eng: Right — two hypotheses: 1) reverse proxy (nginx/ALB) is chunking/transferring and splitting packets; 2) SDK/client is parsing each event as a full JSON message rather than accumulating until complete.

kevin-infra: Ops shows an nginx config on ACME side with proxy_buffering on and small proxy_buffers values. That can fragment large responses. Also ALB idle timeouts can close mid-stream if there are irregular heartbeats.

jess-cs: Customer says this started after they put our requests behind their internal edge proxy. It used to work when hitting us directly.

alan-eng: Repro plan: 1) curl -N against our staging with a tool call that has >8KB args, 2) run through an nginx reverse proxy with proxy_buffering on and small proxy_buffer_size, 3) verify chunk boundaries. Sample curl to reproduce: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"input":"...very large args...","tool_call":true}' \
  https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/respond?stream=true
```

alan-eng: On the client side, naive pseudocode that fails: `onSSE(data) { JSON.parse(data) }` — bad. Need to accumulate until we have a complete JSON object.

mike-ml: Suggest two fixes (short term + long term):
- short: SDK patch to buffer SSE data chunks and only JSON.parse when a complete JSON is assembled (use brace counting or a streaming JSON parser). Release as a point fix.
- long: change server to mark event boundaries for tool_call payloads (add `event: tool_call_complete` for the final fragment) or prefer sending tool_call args as a single SSE event when they exceed a threshold.

kevin-infra: Also check gateway config — we can set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` correctly and ensure `proxy_buffering off;` on our side for streaming endpoints. But we can't change customer proxies.

jess-cs: For ACME we proposed a temporary workaround: disable streaming for tool_call routes (`stream=false`) or add `X-Redwood-Toolcall-Mode: buffered` header so server returns tool call args in one response. Customer prefers to keep streaming.

sara-support: Attached the minimal failing payload we used to repro in staging: `{"type":"tool_call","tool":"annotate","params":{"text":"` + 12k bytes of sample text + `"}}` — when proxied through nginx with default buffers, the SSE event got split and the parser saw `...\"text\":\"...partial` then crashed.

alan-eng: Error dump from SDK consumer: 
```
Error: SchemaValidationError
  at parse (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/redwood-sdk/lib/stream.js:87:15)
  at onmessage (stream.js:45:7)
  cause: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
```

mike-ml: Immediate action items: 1) ship SDK hotfix v0.34.2 to buffer & validate completeness before parse; 2) add server-side marker `event: tool_call_fragment` + final `event: tool_call_complete` for heavy payloads; 3) docs note: clients must assemble fragments.

alan-eng: I'll open a PR for the SDK change. Proposed simple algorithm: keep a small ring buffer of fragments, append new chunk, attempt parse only if brace-counter is zero and last char is `}` (cheap heuristic). Also add a 10s assemble timeout to surface better error if stream stalls.

kevin-infra: Ops: can we detect on our edge that SSE event size > X and send as a single event? Might be tricky with token-level streaming, but for tool_call args we can buffer server-side up to 64KB then emit one event. Creating a canary rollout for this.

ops-bot: Incident INC-1243 opened for ACME streaming toolcall truncation. Priority P2.

jess-cs: I'll message the customer with temporary steps: disable streaming for bulk tool args or route through direct endpoint (bypass internal edge), and we'll coordinate a patch window.

sara-support: Thanks. One more note: customer observed truncation only when checksum/meta nested object present, so nested JSON depth + large strings seems to correlate. Probably just payload size + proxy fragmentation.

mike-ml: Once SDK fix is out we'll push a minor server change to add `event` markers — that will make client assembly trivial.

alan-eng: ETA for SDK hotfix: 4 hours. Will include unit tests that simulate splitting JSON across multiple SSE events at arbitrary byte boundaries.

jess-cs: Customer ok with SDK hotfix + canary server change. I'll schedule a customer call for tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sara-support: Great — marking as in-progress. Adding links: INC-1243, PR#789 (SDK buffer), CHAN: #release-hotfix.

kevin-infra: Follow-up: also audit gateways for `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_temp_file_size` recommendations in our troubleshooting guide.

sara-support: Thanks everyone — will update ticket when SDK v0.34.2 is published.

(ops-bot): Note: automatic rollback enabled for canary if error rate on streaming endpoints increases by >2%.
